definition_zh: 安排；筹备；整理；排列；商定；改编（乐曲）
definition_en: to plan or organize something, to put objects in a particular order, to settle terms with someone, or to adapt a piece of music for performance
core_image: 把散落的物件一件件摆到各自该在的位置
scene: 婚礼前一天的教堂里，志愿者正把长椅和花束一一摆到合适的位置。Volunteers spent the afternoon arranging chairs for the wedding.
sceneCN: 这里 arrange 是「整理、排列、布置」（第 2 个义项：把物件按顺序或位置摆好）；句意为「志愿者花了一下午为婚礼摆放椅子」。画面中有长椅、花束与来回走动的志愿者。

pos.zh: 动词：安排；筹备；整理；排列；商定；改编（乐曲）

derivatives.zh: 由 arrange 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「安排；布局；协议；改编曲」
由 arrange 加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「安排者；乐曲改编者」
由前缀 re- 加 arrange 构成，义为「重新安排；重新排列」

senses.title: To plan and organize something
senses.definition: to plan and organize an event, meeting, or course of action in advance
senses.definitionCN: 预先计划并组织活动、会议或行动步骤
senses.example: They arranged a meeting for Friday morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把会议安排在周五上午。
senses.why: The word first meant setting things in a row; planning is putting events in their proper row ahead of time.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初表示把东西排成行；计划就是提前把一件件事排到它们该在的位置上。

senses.title: To put things in a neat order
senses.definition: to place objects in a particular order or position, often so that they look neat
senses.definitionCN: 把物件按特定顺序或位置摆放，通常是为了整齐好看
senses.example: She arranged the books by size, tallest on the left.
senses.exampleCN: 她按大小把书排好，最高的放在左边。
senses.why: This is the literal row: the hands move each object until the whole set lines up.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的「排成行」：双手把每件东西移动到位，直到整套都对齐。

senses.title: To settle terms with someone
senses.definition: to come to an agreement about the details of something with another person or group
senses.definitionCN: 与另一人或团体就某事的细节达成一致
senses.example: We arranged a loan with the local bank.
senses.exampleCN: 我们与当地银行商定了一笔贷款。
senses.why: Two parties are like two rows of items; the terms are settled once both sides line up.
senses.whyCN: 双方就像两排物件；当两边都对齐时，条款也就谈妥了。

senses.title: To adapt music for performance
senses.definition: to change a piece of music so that it can be performed by different instruments or voices
senses.definitionCN: 改写乐曲，使其能由不同的乐器或人声演奏
senses.example: The composer arranged the folk song for a small orchestra.
senses.exampleCN: 作曲家把这首民歌改编成小编制管弦乐。
senses.why: Notes, like objects, are taken apart and set into a new order that suits the new performers.
senses.whyCN: 音符也像物件一样被拆开，再按适合新演奏者的方式重新排好。

intro.en: Arrange reaches English through French, but its root ring comes from Frankish, so the word carries a Germanic core inside a French shape.
intro.cn: arrange 经由法语进入英语，但它的词根「环、圈」来自法兰克语，因此这个词是法语外形包着日耳曼内核。

items.en: 「*hringaz」 is reconstructed as 'ring, circle', a shape word shared by several Germanic languages.
items.cn: 「*hringaz」被重构为「环、圈」，这是多个日耳曼语言共有的形状词。

items.en: Frankish 「*hring」 kept the ring sense, but how the meaning moved from a circle to a row is source uncertain.
items.cn: 法兰克语「*hring」保留「环」义，但意义如何从圆圈转到一排，来源存疑。

items.en: Arengier meant 'to put in a row, set in order'; the a- is a weakened form of Latin ad 'to'.
items.cn: arengier 意为「排成行、摆整齐」；其中 a- 是拉丁语 ad「向」的弱化形式。

items.en: Arranger carried the row image onward and added the senses of settling a matter and fitting out a plan.
items.cn: arranger 延续了「排成行」的形象，又添上「谈妥事情」与「筹划」的意思。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fourteenth century, first for placing things and later for planning.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个动词，先用于摆放物件，后用于筹划事情。

items.en: The musical sense is the newest branch: notes are reordered just as objects were.
items.cn: 音乐义是最晚长出的分枝：音符被重新排序，正如当年的物件。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words close to arrange in spelling or sound; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of planning and putting in order.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写或读音与 arrange 接近的词；近义组收表示计划与整理的一类动词。

entries.definition: A noun or verb for a line of things, or for the extent covered by something.

entries.definition: To bring people or parts together into a working whole.

entries.definition: To make something ready for use or for an event.

entries.definition: To group things by kind or put them in order.

entries.definition: To set a time and place for an event.
entries.definitionCN: 为某件事定下时间和地点。

root: arrange 经由古法语 arengier「排成行」进入英语，a- 是拉丁语 ad「向」的弱化形式，词根 rang 意为「一排、一列」，更早可追到法兰克语表「环、圈」的词。本义就是「把东西排成行」，由此长出三层意思：把事件排好是安排、筹备，把物件排好是整理、布置，把条款排齐是商定；音乐上的改编则是把音符重新排一遍。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses grow out of one gesture: setting things in a row. Events are rowed into a plan, objects into a layout, terms into a deal, and notes into a score.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都从一个动作长出来：把东西排成行。事件排成计划，物件排成布局，条款排成约定，音符排成乐谱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of objects being set one by one into their proper places.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排物件被一件件放到各自该在的位置。

branches.en: THE PLAN LINE: events are placed in their proper order ahead of time.
branches.cn: 计划线：事件被提前放到各自该在的位置。

branches.en: THE ROW LINE: hands move each object until the whole set lines up.
branches.cn: 排列线：双手把每件东西移动到位，直到整套对齐。

branches.en: THE TERMS LINE: two sides line up their conditions.
branches.cn: 条款线：双方把各自的条件排到一致。

branches.en: THE SCORE LINE: notes are reordered for new performers.
branches.cn: 乐谱线：音符为新演奏者重新排序。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY LINE: planning and tidying are the same gesture at different scales.
branches.cn: 日常线：安排与整理是同一动作在不同尺度上的表现。

intro.en: Arrange is a borrowed verb with a Germanic root, so its family is built by inflections, suffixes and the prefix re-.
intro.cn: arrange 是带日耳曼词根的借词，它的词族由屈折变化、后缀与前缀 re- 构成。

latinIntro.en: The root ring is Frankish rather than Latin, so there is no Latin layer to match here.
latinIntro.cn: 词根「环、圈」来自法兰克语而非拉丁语，因此这里没有对应的拉丁层。

senses.title: The act of planning and preparing
senses.definition: the act of planning and organizing something, or the plans that result from it
senses.definitionCN: 计划并组织某件事的行为，或由此形成的计划
senses.example: The travel agency made all the arrangements for us.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行社为我们做好了一切安排。
senses.why: The suffix -ment turns the verb into the thing done: the rows that have been set.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 把动词变成「做完的事」：那些已经排好的行。

senses.title: The way things are laid out
senses.definition: the order or pattern in which objects or elements are placed
senses.definitionCN: 物件或元素被摆放时所形成的顺序与样式
senses.example: The seating arrangement put the two old friends side by side.
senses.exampleCN: 这样的座位安排让两位老朋友坐在了一起。
senses.why: Here the noun names the row itself, seen as a finished shape rather than an action.
senses.whyCN: 这里的名词指「排好的行」本身，被看成完成的形状，而不是一次动作。

senses.title: An agreement between parties
senses.definition: an agreement or understanding reached with another person or group
senses.definitionCN: 与另一人或团体达成的协议或谅解
senses.example: They reached an arrangement with the landlord about the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 他们与房东就租金达成了约定。
senses.why: Two parties are two rows of terms; when both line up, the arrangement exists.
senses.whyCN: 双方就是两排条款；两边对齐时，协议便成立了。

senses.title: A piece of music adapted for performance
senses.definition: a version of a piece of music rewritten for particular instruments, voices, or a performance
senses.definitionCN: 为特定乐器、人声或演出而改写的乐曲版本
senses.example: The orchestra played a jazz arrangement of the old waltz.
senses.exampleCN: 乐团演奏了那首老华尔兹的爵士改编版。
senses.why: The notes were rowed anew, so the noun names the score that came out of that reordering.
senses.whyCN: 音符被重新排过一遍，于是名词指重新排列后产生的乐谱。

intro.en: Arrangement is the noun built on arrange, and it inherits the same row image from a Germanic root by way of French.

items.en: Frankish 「*hring」 kept the ring sense, but the shift from circle to row is source uncertain.
items.cn: 法兰克语「*hring」保留「环」义，但从圆圈到一排的转变来源存疑。

items.en: Arengier meant 'to put in a row'; its noun arengement named the resulting order.
items.cn: arengier 意为「排成行」，其名词 arengement 指排好后的次序。

items.en: Arranger and its noun carried the word into the senses of preparing and agreeing.
items.cn: arranger 及其名词把这个词带入「筹备」与「达成一致」的义域。

items.en: English took the noun in the fifteenth century, keeping both the physical and the planning senses.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个名词，物理排列与计划筹备两义同时保留。

items.en: The musical sense is the latest: a score that has been set in a new order.

items.exampleCN: 文件次序被打乱，让查找变慢了。

definition_zh: 逮捕；拘留；阻止；抑制；吸引（注意）；心脏骤停
definition_en: to seize someone by legal authority, to stop something from continuing, to catch and hold attention, or a sudden stop of the heart
core_image: 一只手从背后按住正要离开的人的肩膀
scene: 巷口的警笛声还没停，两名警员已经堵住了翻墙男子的退路。The officers arrested the man before he could climb the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 arrest 是「逮捕、拘留」（第 1 个义项：依法抓捕某人）；句意为「警员在那名男子翻上墙之前就逮捕了他」。画面中有巷口、警笛与翻墙的人。

pos.zh: 动词：逮捕；拘留；阻止；抑制；吸引（注意）
名词：逮捕；被捕；心脏骤停

derivatives.zh: 由 arrest 加 -ee 构成，义为「被逮捕者」
由前缀 re- 加 arrest 构成，义为「再次逮捕」
由 arrest 加 -ing 构成，义为「引人注目的」

senses.title: To seize someone by legal authority
senses.definition: to take hold of someone and place them in legal custody, usually on a charge
senses.definitionCN: 抓住某人并将其置于合法羁押之下，通常因某项指控
senses.example: The officers arrested the man before he could climb the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 警员在那名男子翻上墙之前就逮捕了他。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to make something stand still, and a person is made to stop by being held.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本义是「使停住」，而人被抓住，就是被强制停下。

senses.title: To stop something from continuing
senses.definition: to stop or slow the course of something such as growth, decay, or movement
senses.definitionCN: 使增长、衰退或运动等过程停下或变慢
senses.example: The new treatment arrested the spread of the infection.
senses.exampleCN: 新的治疗抑制了感染的扩散。
senses.why: Here the object is not a person but a process, and arrest means to make that process stand still.
senses.whyCN: 这里被抓住的不是人而是一个过程，arrest 就是让这个过程停住不动。

senses.title: To catch and hold attention
senses.definition: to attract and hold someone's attention or interest strongly
senses.definitionCN: 强烈地吸引并留住某人的注意力或兴趣
senses.example: Her unusual story arrested everyone's attention.
senses.exampleCN: 她不寻常的经历吸引了所有人的注意。
senses.why: Attention is caught the way a hand catches an arm: once held, it cannot easily move away.
senses.whyCN: 注意力被抓住的方式，就像手抓住手臂：一旦被握住，便不容易移开。

senses.title: A sudden stop of the heart
senses.definition: in cardiac arrest, a condition in which the heart suddenly stops pumping blood
senses.definitionCN: 用于 cardiac arrest，指心脏突然停止泵血的状态
senses.example: A sudden cardiac arrest left him unconscious for several minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 一次突发的心脏骤停让他失去意识好几分钟。
senses.why: The medical phrase takes the plain sense of stopping: the organ simply stands still.
senses.whyCN: 医学短语用的是最朴素的「停住」义：这个器官就是停在那里不动了。

senses.title: The state of being held by police
senses.definition: in the phrase under arrest, the state of being held by the police
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 under arrest，指被警方羁押的状态
senses.example: The suspect remained under arrest until the hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 嫌疑人一直被拘留到听证会举行。
senses.why: The noun names the condition that results once the hand has stopped the person.
senses.whyCN: 名词指的是手把人停住之后所形成的状态。

intro.en: Arrest goes back to a Latin verb for standing still, and every modern sense still carries that idea of being stopped.
intro.cn: arrest 可追到一个表示「站住」的拉丁动词，现代各个义项都还带着「被停住」的意思。

items.en: The root 「*sta-」 meant 'to stand', and it lies behind many Latin words for standing and staying.
items.cn: 词根「*sta-」意为「站立」，拉丁语中许多表示站立与停留的词都由它而来。

items.en: Restare meant 'to remain standing, stay behind'; ad- added the sense of moving toward that stopping point.
items.cn: restare 意为「继续站着、留在后面」，ad- 又添上「朝那个停点靠过去」的意思。

items.en: Arrestare is recorded in the sense 'to stop, hold back', and this is the form that passed into French.
items.cn: arrestare 有「使停下、扣住」的用法，进入法语的就是这一形式。

items.en: Arester meant both 'to stop' and 'to seize', and English took over both.
items.cn: arester 既指「停下」，也指「抓住」，英语把两义一并接收。

items.en: The legal sense of holding a person is recorded early, and the medical phrase cardiac arrest comes much later.
items.cn: 扣押某人的法律义很早就出现，医学术语 cardiac arrest 则要晚得多。

items.en: The word now covers police custody, halted processes, held attention and a stopped heart.
items.cn: 这个词如今涵盖警方羁押、被止住的过程、被抓住的注意力，以及停跳的心脏。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short verbs close to arrest in spelling; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of seizing, detaining and stopping.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写与 arrest 接近的短动词；近义组收表示抓住、扣留与阻止的动词。

entries.definition: A verb or noun for stopping activity and relaxing, from the same Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「休息」，与 arrest 同出拉丁词根。

entries.definition: To state something firmly as true.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「断言、坚称」。

entries.definition: To show or declare that something is true or genuine.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「证明、证实」。

entries.definition: To keep someone in official custody, often while a case is examined.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人置于官方扣留之下，常在案件审查期间。

entries.definition: To take someone or something by force.
entries.definitionCN: 以武力抓住某人或某物。

entries.definition: To take hold of something quickly and firmly.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速而有力地抓住某物。

entries.definition: To stop, or to cause something to stop.
entries.definitionCN: 停止，或使某物停止。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a hand on the shoulder to halted growth, held attention and a stopped heart.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子从按在肩上的手，走到被止住的增长、被抓住的注意力与停跳的心脏。

normal.en: A hand on the shoulder: the person is made to stand still.
normal.cn: 一只手按在肩上：这个人被迫站住。

normal.en: Police arrest: the state stops the person's movement.
normal.cn: 警方逮捕：国家让这个人不能再走动。

normal.en: Arrest a process: growth stands still.
normal.cn: 抑制一个过程：增长停在那里。

normal.en: Arrest attention: the eyes stop and turn.
normal.cn: 吸引注意：目光停住并转过来。

normal.en: Cardiac arrest: the heart itself stops.
normal.cn: 心脏骤停：心脏本身停了下来。

abstract.en: The core idea is making something stand still.
abstract.cn: 核心意思是让某样东西停住不动。

abstract.en: The same word stops people, processes, eyes and a heart.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能让人的脚步、进程、目光乃至心脏停下。

abstract.en: Legal custody is only one form of that stopping.
abstract.cn: 法律上的羁押只是这种「停住」的一种形式。

examples.en: The officers arrested the man before he could climb the wall.
examples.cn: 警员在那名男子翻上墙之前就逮捕了他。

examples.en: A sudden cardiac arrest left him unconscious for several minutes.
examples.cn: 一次突发的心脏骤停让他失去意识好几分钟。

examples.en: Her unusual story arrested everyone's attention.
examples.cn: 她不寻常的经历吸引了所有人的注意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿瑞斯特」——阿瑞斯特在巷口被警员按住肩膀，动弹不得：逮捕

root: arrest 来自拉丁语 ad-（向）加 restare（停住、站住），俗拉丁语 arrestare 意为「使停下」，经古法语 arester 进入英语。本义是让人或物停住，于是有了三层引申：让人停下就是逮捕，让过程停下就是抑制，让目光停下就是吸引注意；医学术语 cardiac arrest 则是心脏本身停跳。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses share one core: making something stand still. A person is held, a process is halted, attention is caught, the heart stops, and custody is the state that follows.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项共享一个核心：让某样东西停住。人被扣住，过程被止住，注意力被抓住，心脏停跳，羁押则是停住之后的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand from behind landing on the shoulder of someone about to leave.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手从背后按在正要离开的人肩上。

branches.en: THE PERSON LINE: legal arrest makes a person stand still.
branches.cn: 人身线：法律上的逮捕让人停住。

branches.en: THE PROCESS LINE: growth and spread are made to stand still.
branches.cn: 过程线：增长与扩散被止住。

branches.en: THE EYE LINE: attention is caught and held in place.
branches.cn: 目光线：注意力被抓住并固定在原处。

branches.en: THE HEART LINE: the organ itself stops pumping.
branches.cn: 心脏线：这个器官自己停止了泵血。

branches.en: THE CUSTODY LINE: once stopped, the person remains in a held state.
branches.cn: 羁押线：一旦被停住，这个人就处在被扣留的状态。

intro.en: Arrest is a Latin verb carried through French; its family adds prefixes and suffixes to the same stopping core.
intro.cn: arrest 是经法语传来的拉丁动词，它的词族围绕同一个「停住」核心加前缀与后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root restare also produced rest and restive, which keep the sense of staying or standing back.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 restare 还生出 rest 与 restive，它们都保留「停留、退后」的意思。

items.example: The guard arrested the man at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 警卫在门口抓住了那名男子。

items.meaning: the third person singular or plural noun
items.example: The city reports several arrests each night.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市每晚都会报告数起逮捕。

items.meaning: the past tense and past participle
items.example: He was arrested near the station.
items.exampleCN: 他在车站附近被捕。

items.meaning: the present participle, or an adjective for something striking
items.meaningCN: 现在分词，或表示「引人注目的」形容词
items.example: The painting has an arresting colour.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画的色彩十分抓眼。

items.meaning: a person who has been arrested
items.example: The arrestee was held overnight.
items.exampleCN: 被逮捕者被拘留了一夜。

items.example: Police rearrested him after the new evidence.
items.exampleCN: 有了新证据后，警方再次逮捕了他。

items.meaning: the act of arresting, or a legal attachment of property
items.meaningCN: 逮捕行为，或法律上的财产扣押
items.example: The arrestment of the ship's cargo was disputed.
items.exampleCN: 对船货的扣押引发了争议。

items.meaning: describing an offence for which a person may be arrested
items.meaningCN: 形容可据以逮捕的罪行
items.example: It is an arrestable offence under the act.
items.exampleCN: 依该法这属于可逮捕的罪行。

latinEntries.meaning: to stop activity and stay still
latinEntries.example: They rested by the river at noon.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 他们中午在河边歇息。

latinEntries.meaning: unable to stay still, restless and impatient
latinEntries.example: The restless crowd grew restive.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 躁动的人群变得越来越不安。

definition_zh: 到达；到来；（新）到达者；新到货；到达大厅
definition_en: the act of reaching a place, the coming of an event or period, a person or thing that has just come, or the part of a building where people arrive
core_image: 列车进站，站台上的人抬起头朝出口走去
scene: 站台的显示屏刚翻到终点站，提着行李的人群朝出口涌去。Her arrival was announced over the loudspeaker.
sceneCN: 这里 arrival 是「到达」（第 1 个义项：抵达某地的行为）；句意为「她的到达通过广播播报了」。画面中有站台、显示屏与提行李的人群。

pos.zh: 名词：到达；到来；到达者；新到货；到达大厅

derivatives.zh: arrival 的动词形式，义为「到达；抵达」
借自法语，由 arriver 加 -iste 构成，义为「暴发户；钻营上位者」

senses.title: The act of reaching a place
senses.definition: the act of reaching a place at the end of a journey
senses.definitionCN: 一段行程结束时抵达某地的行为
senses.example: Her arrival was announced over the loudspeaker.
senses.exampleCN: 她的到达通过广播播报了。
senses.why: The Latin verb first meant to reach the shore, so arrival is literally the moment a journey touches land.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词本义是「到岸」，所以 arrival 字面上就是行程触到陆地的那一刻。

senses.title: The coming of an event or period
senses.definition: the moment when an event, season, or period begins to exist or becomes present
senses.definitionCN: 某个事件、季节或时期开始出现、来临的时刻
senses.example: The arrival of spring brought blossoms to the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 春天的到来让山谷开满了花。
senses.why: Spring is imagined as a traveller: it comes, and its coming is an arrival.
senses.whyCN: 春天被想象成一个旅人：它来了，它的到来就是一次 arrival。

senses.title: A person or thing that has just come
senses.definition: a person or thing that has recently come to a place, often used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 刚刚来到某地的人或物，常以复数形式使用
senses.example: The hotel keeps a list of new arrivals at the front desk.
senses.exampleCN: 酒店在前台保留一份新到客人的名单。
senses.why: By a shift from the act to its result, the arrival becomes the one who has arrived.
senses.whyCN: 由动作转指结果，arrival 便成了「已经到达的那个人」。

senses.title: The place where people arrive
senses.definition: the part of an airport or station where passengers come in
senses.definitionCN: 机场或车站里旅客抵达后走出的区域
senses.example: We waited in the arrival hall for the delayed flight.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在到达大厅等那班延误的航班。
senses.why: The act gives its name to the place built for it, just as other actions name their rooms.
senses.whyCN: 这个动作把自己的名字给了专为它而建的地方，正如别的动作也会给房间命名。

intro.en: Arrival is built on arrive, and both go back to a Latin image of a boat touching the shore.
intro.cn: arrival 建立在 arrive 之上，两者都可追到「船靠岸」这一拉丁意象。

items.en: Ripa meant 'shore, bank', the edge where land meets water.
items.cn: ripa 意为「岸、河岸」，是陆地与水相接的边缘。

items.en: Ad ripa 'to the shore' became the verb arrivare, 'to reach the shore, come to land'.
items.cn: ad ripa「到岸边」合成了动词 arrivare，意为「到岸、靠岸」。

items.en: Ariver kept the travel sense but lost the river: one could now arrive anywhere.
items.cn: ariver 保留了行程义，却丢掉了河流：如今人可以去到任何地方。

items.en: Arrive is recorded in English in the fourteenth century, and arrival is its noun formed with -al.
items.cn: arrive 在十四世纪见于英语，arrival 则是它加后缀 -al 构成的名词。

items.en: The noun widened from the act of reaching land to any coming, and then to those who come and the hall they come through.
items.cn: 这个名词从「靠岸」扩到一切到来，再扩到到来的人与到来的大厅。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words close to arrival in spelling or sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for coming and appearing.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写或读音与 arrival 接近的词；近义组收表示「到来、出现」的词。

entries.definition: A person or group competing with another for the same goal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「竞争者、对手」。

entries.definition: To begin to exist or to come into notice.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「出现、产生」。

entries.definition: The verb that underlies arrival, meaning to reach a place.
entries.definitionCN: arrival 的动词形式，义为「到达某地」。

entries.definition: The approach or arrival of someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 某人或某物的临近与到来。

entries.definition: The act of becoming visible or present.
entries.definitionCN: 露面、出现的行为。

entries.definition: The moment an aircraft or boat reaches the ground or shore.
entries.definitionCN: 飞机或船只触地、靠岸的那一刻。

entries.definition: The act of coming in, or the place through which one comes in.
entries.definitionCN: 进入的行为，或进入时所经过的地方。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow arrival from a train platform to spring, new guests and the arrivals hall.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子让 arrival 从站台走到春天、新到的客人，以及到达大厅。

normal.en: Arrival is the end of a journey touching the platform.
normal.cn: arrival 是一段行程触到站台的那一刻。

normal.en: The arrival of spring: a season walks in.
normal.cn: 春天的到来：一个季节走了进来。

normal.en: New arrivals: the ones who have just come.
normal.cn: 新到者：刚刚到来的人。

normal.en: The arrival hall is named after the act it serves.
normal.cn: 到达大厅因它所服务的那个动作而得名。

normal.en: Arrive once meant to reach the shore.
normal.cn: arrive 曾经只表示「靠岸」。

abstract.en: One noun covers the act, the result, the person and the place.
abstract.cn: 一个名词覆盖了行为、结果、人物与地点。

abstract.en: A journey's last step can name a whole season.
abstract.cn: 行程的最后一步可以为整个季节命名。

abstract.en: The shore image survives inside every arrival.
abstract.cn: 「靠岸」的形象藏在每一次 arrival 里。

examples.en: Her arrival was announced over the loudspeaker.
examples.cn: 她的到达通过广播播报了。

examples.en: The arrival of spring brought blossoms to the valley.
examples.cn: 春天的到来让山谷开满了花。

examples.en: The hotel keeps a list of new arrivals at the front desk.
examples.cn: 酒店在前台保留一份新到客人的名单。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊，来我」——远方的人说「啊，我来啦」，拖着箱子走进到达大厅：到达

root: arrive 来自拉丁语 ad ripa「到岸边」，本指船靠岸，经古法语 ariver 进入英语；arrival 是 arrive 加名词后缀 -al，字面就是「靠岸这件事」。由「靠岸」扩为一切到达，再扩为事件与季节的到来；由动作转指结果，又指到达的人与新到的货物；动作还给专门容纳它的场所命名，于是有了 arrival hall。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses grow from one journey's end: the act of reaching, the coming of an era, the person or thing that comes, and the hall built for coming.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项从一段行程的终点长出来：抵达的动作、时代的到来、到来的人与物，以及为到来而建的厅堂。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a train pulling into a platform while travellers lift their heads toward the exit.
core.cn: 核心意象：列车进站，旅客们抬头朝出口走去。

branches.en: THE JOURNEY LINE: arrival is the moment a trip touches its end.
branches.cn: 行程线：arrival 是旅途触到终点的那一刻。

branches.en: THE SEASON LINE: events and periods are imagined as travellers.
branches.cn: 季节线：事件与时期被想象成旅人。

branches.en: THE GUEST LINE: the act gives its name to the one who performed it.
branches.cn: 来客线：动作把名字给了完成它的人。

branches.en: THE HALL LINE: a place is named after the act it serves.
branches.cn: 大厅线：场所因它所服务的动作而得名。

branches.en: THE WELCOME LINE: every arrival is both an event and a person to greet.
branches.cn: 迎接线：每一次到达既是一个事件，也是一个要迎接的人。

intro.en: Arrival is arrive plus the noun suffix -al, and the verb itself came through French from Latin.
intro.cn: arrival 是 arrive 加名词后缀 -al，动词本身经法语来自拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin word ripa 'shore' also left riparian in English, and the same shore word stands behind river.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ripa「岸」还给英语留下了 riparian，而表示河流的 river 背后也是同一个「岸」字。

items.meaning: the act of reaching a place
items.example: His arrival changed the mood of the room.
items.exampleCN: 他的到来改变了房间里的气氛。

items.example: The board lists all arrivals before noon.
items.exampleCN: 指示牌列出了中午前所有到达的航班。

items.example: They arrive at the hotel around six.
items.exampleCN: 他们大约六点到达酒店。

items.meaning: the past tense and past participle
items.example: The train arrived ten minutes late.
items.exampleCN: 火车晚到了十分钟。

items.example: Guests were arriving all morning.
items.exampleCN: 整个上午客人们陆续到达。

items.meaning: a person who climbs to success by any means
items.meaningCN: 不择手段向上爬的暴发户
items.example: The novel mocks a young arriviste in the capital.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说讽刺了首都里一个年轻的钻营者。

items.meaning: the part of a terminal where passengers come in
items.meaningCN: 航站楼或车站里旅客抵达的区域
items.example: A driver held a sign in the arrival hall.
items.exampleCN: 司机在到达大厅举着一块牌子。

items.meaning: the scheduled moment of reaching a place
items.example: The arrival time is printed on the ticket.
items.exampleCN: 到达时间印在车票上。

latinEntries.meaning: relating to the bank of a river
latinEntries.example: Riparian plants line the quiet stream.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 河岸植物沿着安静的小溪生长。

latinEntries.meaning: a large natural stream of water
latinEntries.example: The river ran brown after the storm.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 暴风雨过后，河水变成了褐色。

definition_zh: 到达；抵达；（时间、阶段）来临；（物品）送达；（在事业上）成功立足
definition_en: to reach a place at the end of a journey, to come at a particular time, to be delivered, or to become successful
core_image: 船头轻轻触到岸边的那一刻
scene: 长途巴士在雨后的清晨驶入小镇车站，车门打开，乘客陆续下车。They arrived at the station just as the rain stopped.
sceneCN: 这里 arrive 是「到达、抵达」（第 1 个义项：行程结束时抵达某地）；句意为「雨刚停时他们到达了车站」。画面中有雨后的小站、长途巴士与下车的乘客。

pos.zh: 动词：到达；抵达；来临；送达；成功立足

derivatives.zh: 由 arrive 加名词后缀 -al 构成，义为「到达；到来；到达者」
借自法语，由 arriver 加 -iste 构成，义为「暴发户；钻营上位者」

senses.title: To reach a place
senses.definition: to reach a place, especially at the end of a journey
senses.definitionCN: 尤指在一段行程结束时抵达某地
senses.example: They arrived at the station just as the rain stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 雨刚停时他们到达了车站。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to reach the shore, so arriving is a journey touching its edge.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词本义是「到岸」，所以 arrive 就是行程触到它的边缘。

senses.title: A time or moment to come
senses.definition: to come at a particular moment or stage, especially one long awaited
senses.definitionCN: 在某个特定的、尤指期待已久的时刻或阶段到来
senses.example: The day we had waited for finally arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 我们等待的那一天终于来临了。
senses.why: Time is pictured as a traveller: the day walks up and reaches us.
senses.whyCN: 时间被描画成一个旅人：那一天走过来，到达了我们面前。

senses.title: To be delivered
senses.definition: to be delivered to a place, as a letter, parcel, or shipment
senses.definitionCN: 信件、包裹或货物被送到某地
senses.example: The letter arrived three days late.
senses.exampleCN: 那封信晚到了三天。
senses.why: Goods also travel, so arriving means the same for a parcel as for a person.
senses.whyCN: 货物同样在旅行，所以包裹的到达与人的到达用的是同一个词。

senses.title: To succeed at last
senses.definition: to reach a position of success or recognition after a period of effort
senses.definitionCN: 经过一段努力后达到成功或被认可的位置
senses.example: After ten years, she finally arrived as a novelist.
senses.exampleCN: 十年之后，她终于成为一位成功的小说家。
senses.why: Success is a destination in this image: the traveller has finally reached it.
senses.whyCN: 在这个意象里成功是一个目的地：旅人终于走到了那里。

intro.en: Arrive still carries the ghost of a boat: the Latin verb meant to reach the shore.
intro.cn: arrive 里还留着一条船的影子：那个拉丁动词本义是「到岸」。

items.en: Ripa meant 'shore, bank', the edge where land meets water.
items.cn: ripa 意为「岸、河岸」，是陆地与水相接的边缘。

items.en: Ad ripa 'to the shore' became arrivare, 'to reach the shore, come to land'.
items.cn: ad ripa「到岸边」合成了 arrivare，意为「到岸、靠岸」。

items.en: Ariver kept the travel sense but dropped the river, so one could arrive anywhere.
items.cn: ariver 保留了行程义，却丢掉了河流，于是人可以去到任何地方。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fourteenth century and widened it to any kind of reaching.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个动词，并把它扩展到一切意义上的「到达」。

items.en: Later uses add time, parcels and careers: a day, a letter and a writer can all arrive.
items.cn: 后来的用法添上时间、包裹与事业：一天、一封信、一位作家都可以 arrive。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words close to arrive in spelling or sound; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of reaching and coming.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写或读音与 arrive 接近的词；近义组收表示「到达、来到」的动词。

entries.definition: To begin to exist or come into notice.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「出现、产生」。

entries.definition: To obtain something from a source, or to originate from it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「取得、源自」。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of reaching a place.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「到达」，是 arrive 的名词形式。

entries.definition: To get to a place or point after travelling or stretching.
entries.definitionCN: 经过行进或伸展后到达某地或某点。

entries.definition: To move toward the speaker or a stated place.
entries.definitionCN: 朝说话者或某一指定地点移动。

entries.definition: To come down to the ground after flight.
entries.definitionCN: 飞行之后落到地面。

entries.definition: To enter a place, especially a vehicle or building.
entries.definitionCN: 进入某处，尤指车辆或建筑。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow arrive from a bus at a station to a long-awaited day, a letter and a career.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子让 arrive 从进站的巴士走到期待已久的日子、一封信与一番事业。

normal.en: Arrive once meant to touch the shore.
normal.cn: arrive 曾经只表示「触到岸边」。

normal.en: The bus arrives: the journey touches the platform.
normal.cn: 巴士到站：行程触到了站台。

normal.en: A day arrives: time walks up to you.
normal.cn: 某一天到来：时间走到你面前。

normal.en: A letter arrives: paper also travels.
normal.cn: 信到了：纸也在旅行。

normal.en: An artist arrives: the career reaches its port.
normal.cn: 艺术家成名：事业抵达了它的港口。

abstract.en: Arriving is always a journey meeting an edge.
abstract.cn: 到达永远是行程碰上一个边缘。

abstract.en: The same verb serves people, time, post and fame.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词服务着人、时间、信件与名声。

abstract.en: The shore image fades but never disappears.
abstract.cn: 「岸」的形象会淡去，却从未消失。

examples.en: They arrived at the station just as the rain stopped.
examples.cn: 雨刚停时他们到达了车站。

examples.en: The letter arrived three days late.
examples.cn: 那封信晚到了三天。

examples.en: After ten years, she finally arrived as a novelist.
examples.cn: 十年之后，她终于成为一位成功的小说家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊，来我」——旅人对着岸边喊「啊，我来啦」，船头正好触岸：到达

root: arrive 来自拉丁语 ad ripa「到岸边」，本指船靠岸，经古法语 ariver 进入英语。由「靠岸」扩为一切抵达：人到达某地、时间来临、物品送达、事业走到成功的位置。词根 ripa「岸」还留在 riparian「河岸的」里，river 背后也是同一个「岸」字。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of arrive are one journey reaching an edge: a person reaches a place, time reaches us, a parcel reaches a door, and a career reaches success.
sensesIntro.cn: arrive 的四个义项都是行程触到某个边缘：人到了地方，时间到了眼前，包裹到了门口，事业到了成功处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boat's bow lightly touching the bank.
core.cn: 核心意象：船头轻轻触到岸边。

branches.en: THE TRAVEL LINE: a person reaches a place after a journey.
branches.cn: 行程线：人在一段旅途之后到达某地。

branches.en: THE TIME LINE: a moment walks up to the speaker.
branches.cn: 时间线：某个时刻走到说话者面前。

branches.en: THE POST LINE: a parcel makes its own small journey.
branches.cn: 信件线：包裹也在走自己的一小段路。

branches.en: THE CAREER LINE: success is the port a long effort finally reaches.
branches.cn: 事业线：成功是长久努力最终抵达的港口。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY LINE: people and parcels both arrive at a door.
branches.cn: 日常线：人与包裹最后都到达某一扇门前。

intro.en: Arrive came through French from Latin, and its family grows by inflections and the noun suffix -al.
intro.cn: arrive 经法语来自拉丁语，它的词族由屈折变化与名词后缀 -al 扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin shore word ripa also gave English riparian, and the same source stands behind river.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语里表示岸的 ripa 还给英语留下了 riparian，而 river 背后也是同一来源。

items.example: We arrive before dark.
items.exampleCN: 我们在天黑前到达。

items.example: The early train arrives at six.
items.exampleCN: 早班列车六点到达。

items.example: Guests are arriving at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 客人们正陆续到达门口。

items.meaning: the past tense and past participle
items.example: They arrived on a cold morning.
items.exampleCN: 他们在一个寒冷的早晨到达。

items.meaning: the act of reaching a place
items.example: The arrival of the guests surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 客人们的到来让我们很意外。

items.example: The list of arrivals filled a page.
items.exampleCN: 到达名单写满了一页。

items.meaning: a person who rises by pushing others aside
items.example: The arriviste had no old friends left.
items.exampleCN: 那个钻营者身边已没有老朋友。

items.meaning: the scheduled moment of reaching a place
items.example: Check the arrival time on the board.
items.exampleCN: 看一下公告牌上的到达时间。

latinEntries.exampleCN: 河岸的树木为溪水遮阴。

definition_zh: 艺术；美术；艺术作品；技艺；人文学科；心机、手腕
definition_en: creative work such as painting or sculpture, the works produced by it, a skill, the humanities, or cunning
core_image: 画室里沾着颜料的画笔与一幅还没干透的画布
scene: 午后的画室里弥漫着松节油的气味，画布上的颜色还没有干透。She studied art in Paris for four years.
sceneCN: 这里 art 是「艺术、美术」（第 1 个义项：绘画、雕塑等创造性活动与门类）；句意为「她在巴黎学了四年美术」。画面中有画室、画笔与未干的画布。

pos.zh: 名词：艺术；美术；艺术作品；技艺；人文学科；心机

derivatives.zh: 由 art 加 -ist 构成，义为「艺术家；画家」
由 artist 加 -ic 构成，义为「艺术的；有艺术气质的」
由 artist 加 -ry 构成，义为「艺术技巧；艺术性」
由 art 加 -ful 构成，义为「巧妙的；狡黠的」
由 art 加 -less 构成，义为「朴实的；不造作的」

senses.title: Creative work and its field
senses.definition: creative activity such as painting, sculpture, or drawing, and the field in which it is practised
senses.definitionCN: 绘画、雕塑、素描等创造性活动，以及从事这类活动的领域
senses.example: She studied art in Paris for four years.
senses.exampleCN: 她在巴黎学了四年美术。
senses.why: Latin ars meant skill of the hand, and the making of beautiful things became the most famous form of that skill.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ars 意为「手上的技艺」，而制造美的东西成了这种技艺最著名的形态。

senses.title: The works produced
senses.definition: paintings, sculptures, and other works produced by creative activity, considered as a group
senses.definitionCN: 创造性活动产出的绘画、雕塑等作品的总称
senses.example: The gallery shows modern art from Asia.
senses.exampleCN: 这家画廊展出亚洲的现代艺术作品。
senses.why: By a common shift, the name of the activity passes to what the activity leaves behind.
senses.whyCN: 按常见的转指规律，活动的名称会转到这项活动留下的作品上。

senses.title: A skill or knack
senses.definition: a skill or ability, especially one gained by practice, as in the art of conversation
senses.definitionCN: 尤指通过练习获得的技能或本领，如谈话的技巧
senses.example: He has mastered the art of polite refusal.
senses.exampleCN: 他掌握了礼貌拒绝的技巧。
senses.why: Before it meant beauty, ars meant any trained skill, and that older sense survives in phrases such as the art of war.
senses.whyCN: 在表示美之前，ars 本指任何训练得来的技艺，这一旧义活在「战争的艺术」这类短语里。

senses.title: The humanities
senses.definition: in the plural arts, subjects such as history, literature, and languages, contrasted with the sciences
senses.definitionCN: 用复数 arts 指历史、文学、语言等学科，与理科相对
senses.example: She chose arts over science at university.
senses.exampleCN: 她在大学选择了文科而不是理科。
senses.why: The liberal arts were the skills once thought fit for a free citizen, and the label stayed on those school subjects.
senses.whyCN: 自由技艺曾是被认为适合自由公民学习的技能，这个标签留在了这些学校科目上。

senses.title: Cunning or trickery
senses.definition: in older or literary use, cunning or crafty behaviour, surviving chiefly in artful and artifice
senses.definitionCN: 较古旧或文学性的用法，指狡黠、算计的行为，主要残留在 artful 与 artifice 里
senses.example: The old fox won by art, not by strength.
senses.exampleCN: 那只老狐狸靠心机而不是力气取胜。
senses.why: Skill can be used to deceive, so the same word that praised a craftsman could also name a trickster's craft.
senses.whyCN: 技艺可以用来欺骗，因此赞美工匠的那个词也能指骗子的手段。

intro.en: Art comes from a Latin word for skill of any kind; beauty and cunning are both branches of that skill.
intro.cn: art 来自一个表示各种「技艺」的拉丁词；美与狡黠都是这种技艺的分枝。

items.en: A root often reconstructed as 「*h₂er-」 meant 'to fit together', the kind of joining a craftsman does. The exact form and its spread are source uncertain.
items.cn: 常被重构为「*h₂er-」的词根意为「拼合、使接合」，正是工匠所做的连接。确切形式与传播来源存疑。

items.en: Ars, genitive artis, meant 'skill, craft, technique', whether of a carpenter, a speaker, or a physician.
items.cn: ars（属格 artis）意为「技艺、手艺、技巧」，无论木匠、演说家还是医生的本领都可用它。

items.en: The phrase artes liberales named the liberal arts, the studies thought worthy of a free person.
items.cn: artes liberales 即「自由技艺」，指被认为配得上自由人身份的那些学问。

items.en: Old French art kept both the skill sense and the growing sense of beautiful making.
items.cn: 古法语 art 既保留了「技艺」义，也带着「美的创造」这一渐长的意思。

items.en: English took the word early, and by the eighteenth century fine art was a settled category.
items.cn: 英语很早就借入这个词，到十八世纪「美术」已经成为稳定的类别。

items.en: The plural arts now labels the humanities, while the cunning sense retreats into artful and artifice.
items.cn: 复数 arts 如今指人文学科，而「心机」义退进了 artful 与 artifice 里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words close to art in spelling; the near-meaning group gathers words for craft, beauty and making.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写与 art 接近的短词；近义组收表示技艺、美与创作的词。

entries.definition: A small insect that lives in an organized colony.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蚂蚁」，一种成群而居的小昆虫。

entries.definition: A curved line or path.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「弧、弧线」。

entries.definition: Suitable or likely to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「恰当的」或「易于……的」。

entries.definition: A skill in making things by hand, or the activity of making them.
entries.definitionCN: 手工制作的技艺，或从事手工制作的活动。

entries.definition: The ability to do something well, gained by training.
entries.definitionCN: 通过训练获得的、把某事做好的能力。

entries.definition: The art of putting paint on a surface, or a picture so made.
entries.definitionCN: 在表面上涂绘的艺术，或这样画出的画。

entries.definition: The planning of how something will look or work.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物的外观或运作方式的规划。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a brush on canvas to trained skill, school subjects and a cunning trick.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子从画布上的画笔，走到练就的技艺、学校科目与狡黠的手段。

normal.en: Art begins with a brush on a wet canvas.
normal.cn: art 从画笔落在未干的画布上开始。

normal.en: Art is also the works hanging on the wall.
normal.cn: art 也是挂在墙上的那些作品。

normal.en: The art of conversation is a trained skill.
normal.cn: 谈话的艺术是一种练出来的技巧。

normal.en: The arts at school means history and literature.
normal.cn: 学校里的 arts 指历史与文学。

normal.en: Art can also mean a trickster's craft.
normal.cn: art 也能指骗子那套手腕。

abstract.en: Skill is the trunk; beauty, subjects and cunning are branches.
abstract.cn: 技艺是树干，美、学科与狡黠是分枝。

abstract.en: The activity and its products share one name.
abstract.cn: 活动与它的产物共用一个名字。

abstract.en: A word for making can always shade into a word for tricking.
abstract.cn: 一个表示制作的词，总能滑向表示欺骗的意思。

examples.en: She studied art in Paris for four years.
examples.cn: 她在巴黎学了四年美术。

examples.en: The gallery shows modern art from Asia.
examples.cn: 这家画廊展出亚洲的现代艺术作品。

examples.en: He has mastered the art of polite refusal.
examples.cn: 他掌握了礼貌拒绝的技巧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿特」——阿特在画室里洗画笔，满手都是颜料：艺术

root: art 来自拉丁语 ars（属格 artis），本义是「技艺、手艺」，无论木匠、演说家还是医生的本领都可用它。由「练就的技艺」分出两支：一支走向美的创造，成为绘画、雕塑等「美术」及其作品；一支保留「本领」义，于是有「谈话的艺术」；学校里沿用 artes liberales「自由技艺」之名，以复数 arts 指人文学科；技艺若用于欺骗，则又成了「心机、手腕」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses share one trunk, the Latin word for skill: beauty, its works, trained knack, school subjects, and cunning.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项共享同一个树干，即拉丁语里表示技艺的词：美、美的作品、练就的本领、学校科目，以及狡黠。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a paint-covered brush resting beside a canvas that is still wet.
core.cn: 核心意象：沾满颜料的画笔放在一幅还没干的画布旁。

branches.en: THE STUDIO LINE: creative activity itself is the first sense.
branches.cn: 画室线：创造性活动本身是最先的意思。

branches.en: THE GALLERY LINE: the activity passes its name to the works.
branches.cn: 画廊线：活动把自己的名字给了作品。

branches.en: THE SKILL LINE: any trained ability, not only beauty, is art.
branches.cn: 技艺线：任何练就的本领都算 art，不只限于美。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL LINE: the liberal arts became the humanities.
branches.cn: 学校线：自由技艺变成了人文学科。

branches.en: THE TRICK LINE: skill turned toward deceit becomes cunning.
branches.cn: 诡计线：技艺转向欺骗，就成了心机。

intro.en: Art is a Latin root word, and its large family is built with -ist, -istic, -ry, -ful and -less.
intro.cn: art 是拉丁词根词，它庞大的词族由 -ist、-istic、-ry、-ful 与 -less 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun ars also lies behind artisan and artifact, both built on the idea of making.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁名词 ars 还藏在 artisan 与 artifact 背后，两者都建立在「制作」这一概念上。

items.meaningCN: 技艺、手艺或创造性作品
items.example: Art can be made from almost anything.
items.exampleCN: 艺术几乎可以用任何材料创作。

items.meaningCN: 复数形式，或指人文学科
items.example: The arts faculty stands by the library.
items.exampleCN: 文学院就在图书馆旁。

items.example: The artist signed the canvas.
items.exampleCN: 艺术家在画布上签了名。

items.meaningCN: 与艺术或艺术家有关的
items.example: The room has an artistic feel.
items.exampleCN: 这个房间有一种艺术气息。

items.example: Her artistry showed in every line.
items.exampleCN: 她的艺术功力在每一笔里都看得见。

items.meaning: clever, sometimes in a cunning way
items.example: He told an artful story to avoid blame.
items.exampleCN: 他编了一套巧妙的说辞来推脱责任。

items.example: Her artless manner won them over.
items.exampleCN: 她毫不做作的样子赢得了他们的好感。

items.meaning: a work of art, or the pictures in a publication
items.meaningCN: 一件艺术品，或出版物中的插图
items.example: The magazine's artwork was bold.
items.exampleCN: 这本杂志的插图很大胆。

latinEntries.meaning: a skilled worker who makes things by hand
latinEntries.meaningCN: 手工制作器物的熟练工匠
latinEntries.example: The artisan shaped the bowl by hand.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 工匠用手塑成了这只碗。

latinEntries.meaning: an object made by human hands
latinEntries.example: The museum displayed a stone artifact.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 博物馆展出了一件石制器物。

definition_zh: 文章；报道；冠词；物品；条款；条文
definition_en: a piece of writing in a newspaper or magazine, a word such as the or a in grammar, a single item, or a clause in a document
core_image: 杂志页面上被红笔圈出的一个小方块
scene: 清晨的书桌上摊着刚送来的杂志，红笔在其中一页画了个圈。He read the article twice before breakfast.
sceneCN: 这里 article 是「文章、报道」（第 1 个义项：报刊上的一篇非虚构文字）；句意为「他把那篇文章读了两遍才吃早饭」。画面中有杂志、红笔与清晨的书桌。

pos.zh: 名词：文章；报道；冠词；物品；条款；条文

derivatives.zh: 与 article 同出拉丁词根 articulus「关节」，义为「清晰表达；使接合」
由 articulate 加 -ion 构成，义为「发音；关节连接」
由 article 加 -ed 构成，义为「按学徒契约受雇的」

senses.title: A piece of writing in a publication
senses.definition: a piece of writing about a particular subject in a newspaper, magazine, or website
senses.definitionCN: 报刊、杂志或网站上关于某一主题的一篇文字
senses.example: He read the article twice before breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 他把那篇文章读了两遍才吃早饭。
senses.why: Latin articulus meant a small joint or division, and a written piece was seen as one division of a larger text.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 articulus 意为「小关节、小分段」，一篇文章被看成整份文字中的一个分段。

senses.title: A grammatical word
senses.definition: a word such as the, a, or an placed before a noun to show whether it is definite or indefinite
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前、表示确定或不确定的词，如 the、a、an
senses.example: In English, the word the is a definite article.
senses.exampleCN: 在英语里，the 这个词是定冠词。
senses.why: Grammarians treated these little words as small joints attaching a noun to its sentence.
senses.whyCN: 语法学家把这些小词看作把名词接到句子上的小关节。

senses.title: A single item or object
senses.definition: a particular object or item, especially one of a class of goods
senses.definitionCN: 某件具体的物品，尤指同类商品中的一件
senses.example: Every article of clothing was packed in plastic.
senses.exampleCN: 每一件衣物都用塑料袋装好了。
senses.why: An item is also a separate division of a stock, so the joint sense fits a single object on a shelf.
senses.whyCN: 一件物品也是一批存货中的一个单位，「关节」义同样能安到货架上的单个物件上。

senses.title: A clause in a document
senses.definition: a separate part of a legal document, contract, or treaty
senses.definitionCN: 法律文件、合同或条约中独立的一条
senses.example: Article five of the treaty limits the fleet.
senses.exampleCN: 条约第五条限制了舰队规模。
senses.why: A long document is divided into numbered joints, and each joint is an article.
senses.whyCN: 长文件被分成编号的关节，每一节就是一条 article。

intro.en: Article goes back to a Latin word for a small joint, and everything it names is a separate part of a larger whole.
intro.cn: article 可追到一个表示「小关节」的拉丁词，它命名的每样东西都是更大整体中的一个独立部分。

items.en: The stem behind Latin artus 'joint' is often reconstructed as 「*h₂er-」, 'to fit together'. The precise form is source uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 artus「关节」背后的词干常被重构为「*h₂er-」，意为「拼合」。确切形式来源存疑。

items.en: Articulus was a small joint or a small division, a diminutive of artus 'joint'.
items.cn: articulus 意为「小关节、小分段」，是 artus「关节」的指小形式。

items.en: In grammar and law the word came to mean a small connecting part: a clause or a short section.
items.cn: 在语法与法律中，这个词转指「小的连接部分」：一条条款或一个短段落。

items.en: Old French article carried the legal and grammatical senses into English.
items.cn: 古法语 article 把法律义与语法义一并带入英语。

items.en: English used article for a clause first; the newspaper sense is much later.
items.cn: 英语最早用 article 指条款；报刊文章义要晚得多。

items.en: The word now covers news pieces, grammar words, goods and treaty clauses.
items.cn: 这个词如今涵盖新闻文章、语法冠词、商品与条约条款。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words sharing the joint root or a similar shape; the near-meaning group gathers essays, reports, clauses and items.
note.cn: 形近组收共享「关节」词根或外形相近的词；近义组收文章、报道、条款与物件。

entries.definition: A very small piece of matter, or a short grammatical word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「微粒」或语法上的「小品词」。

entries.definition: Able to express ideas clearly, or to speak them clearly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或动词，义为「表达清晰的」或「清晰地说出」。

entries.definition: A clever trick or device used to deceive.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「诡计、巧妙的手法」。

entries.definition: A short piece of writing on a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 关于某一主题的短文。

entries.definition: A written or spoken account of an event or situation.
entries.definitionCN: 对事件或情况的书面或口头记述。

entries.definition: A separate part of a legal document or a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 法律文件或句子中的一个独立部分。

entries.definition: A single thing in a list or a group.
entries.definitionCN: 清单或一组事物中的单项。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow article from a marked page to a grammar word, a single item and a treaty clause.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子让 article 从被圈出的页面走到语法冠词、单件物品与条约条款。

normal.en: An article is one section cut from a larger page.
normal.cn: 一篇文章就是从大页面里切出来的一节。

normal.en: The definite article is a small joint before a noun.
normal.cn: 定冠词是名词前的一个小关节。

normal.en: An article of clothing is one item on a shelf.
normal.cn: 一件衣服就是货架上的一件物品。

normal.en: A treaty article is a numbered joint in a text.
normal.cn: 条约条款是文本中编号的一节。

normal.en: All four senses are parts of a bigger whole.
normal.cn: 四个义项都是更大整体中的一部分。

abstract.en: The word for a joint became the word for a section.
abstract.cn: 表示关节的词变成了表示分段的词。

abstract.en: Grammar and law both use joints to divide long things.
abstract.cn: 语法与法律都用「关节」来切分庞杂的东西。

abstract.en: A page, a shelf and a treaty all break into articles.
abstract.cn: 一页纸、一排货架、一份条约都能分成 article。

examples.en: He read the article twice before breakfast.
examples.cn: 他把那篇文章读了两遍才吃早饭。

examples.en: In English, the word the is a definite article.
examples.cn: 在英语里，the 这个词是定冠词。

examples.en: Every article of clothing was packed in plastic.
examples.cn: 每一件衣物都用塑料袋装好了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿提扣」——阿提扣下杂志上的一篇文章，折了个角：文章

root: article 来自拉丁语 articulus，本义「小关节、小分段」，是 artus「关节」的指小形式。一件大东西被分成关节，每一节就是一条文；一篇文章是一份刊物里的一节，条约条款是法律文件的一节，冠词是句子中把名词接上去的小关节，一件物品则是整批货物中的一节。英语最早用 article 指条款，报刊文章义出现得晚得多。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses are all sections of something larger: a page's piece of writing, a grammar word joining a noun, one item among goods, and one clause of a document.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都是更大整体中的一节：页面上的一篇文章、句中连接名词的冠词、货物中的一件物品，以及文件中的一条条文。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small box circled in red on a magazine page.
core.cn: 核心意象：杂志页面上被红笔圈出的一个小方块。

branches.en: THE PAGE LINE: a written piece is one section of a larger text.
branches.cn: 页面线：一篇文字是整份文本中的一个分段。

branches.en: THE GRAMMAR LINE: a small word joins a noun to its sentence.
branches.cn: 语法线：一个小词把名词接到句子上。

branches.en: THE GOODS LINE: an item is one unit cut from a stock.
branches.cn: 货物线：一件物品是一批存货中切出的一件。

branches.en: THE LAW LINE: a treaty is jointed into numbered articles.
branches.cn: 法律线：条约被分成编号的条款。

branches.en: THE TEXT LINE: page and law both divide writing into articles.
branches.cn: 文本线：页面与法律都把文字分成一条一条。

intro.en: Article is a Latin noun; its family grows through the joint root, with suffixes such as -ed, -ate and -ation.
intro.cn: article 是拉丁名词，它的词族通过「关节」这一词根、借助 -ed、-ate 与 -ation 等后缀扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin joint word articulus also produced articulate and articulation, which keep the image of parts joined together.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示关节的 articulus 还生出 articulate 与 articulation，它们都保留「部件接合」的形象。

items.meaning: a small joint, a section or clause
items.meaningCN: 小关节；一个分段或条款
items.example: The article on the front page caused a stir.
items.exampleCN: 头版那篇文章引起了轰动。

items.example: The journal publishes articles every month.
items.exampleCN: 这份期刊每月刊登文章。

items.meaning: bound by a written contract, especially as an apprentice
items.meaningCN: 按书面契约受雇的，尤指学徒
items.example: He was articled to a firm of lawyers.
items.exampleCN: 他与一家律师事务所签了学徒契约。

items.meaning: to express clearly, or to join into a whole
items.meaningCN: 清晰表达，或连接成一个整体
items.example: She can articulate a difficult idea simply.
items.exampleCN: 她能把复杂的想法讲得很简单。

items.meaning: clear speech, or the joining of parts
items.meaningCN: 清晰的发音，或部件的接合
items.example: His articulation improved with practice.
items.exampleCN: 经过练习，他的发音清晰了。

items.meaning: relating to the organs that produce speech
items.example: The chart shows articulatory positions.
items.exampleCN: 这张图展示了发音部位。

items.example: He was inarticulate with anger.
items.exampleCN: 他气得说不出话来。

items.example: Fair play is an article of faith for them.
items.exampleCN: 公平竞争是他们的信条。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 关节分明，因而发音清晰
latinEntries.example: An articulate speaker holds a room.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 一个表达清晰的演讲者能镇住全场。

latinEntries.meaning: the act of jointing or speaking clearly
latinEntries.meaningCN: 接合或清晰发音的行为
latinEntries.example: The articulation of the parts took care.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 各部分的接合需要细心处理。

definition_zh: 人造的；人工的；虚假的；做作的；人为造成的
definition_en: made by people rather than nature, produced to imitate something natural, insincere, or caused by human action
core_image: 橱窗里过分整齐的花，每片叶子都像从模具里压出来
scene: 花店的橱窗里摆着一束颜色过分均匀的玫瑰，走近才发现花瓣是塑料的。The bouquet looked real until she noticed the artificial petals.
sceneCN: 这里 artificial 是「人造的、非天然的」（第 1 个义项：由人制造而非自然生成）；句意为「那束花看上去很真，直到她注意到人造花瓣」。画面中有橱窗、玫瑰与塑料质感的花瓣。

pos.zh: 形容词：人造的；人工的；虚假的；做作的；人为造成的

derivatives.zh: 由 artificial 加 -ly 构成，义为「人工地；人为地」
由 artificial 加 -ity 构成，义为「人造性；不自然；做作」

senses.title: Made by people, not nature
senses.definition: made by human beings rather than occurring naturally
senses.definitionCN: 由人制造，而非自然生成的
senses.example: The bouquet looked real until she noticed the artificial petals.
senses.exampleCN: 那束花看上去很真，直到她注意到人造花瓣。
senses.why: The Latin phrase meant made by art, and art once covered every skilled craft, so anything crafted is artificial.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁短语意为「用技艺做成」，而技艺曾涵盖一切手艺，因此凡经人手制作的都是 artificial。

senses.title: Made to imitate nature
senses.definition: produced by human technology to do the work of something natural
senses.definitionCN: 用人类技术制造，以替代某种天然之物的功能
senses.example: Artificial light kept the plants growing all winter.
senses.exampleCN: 人造光让这些植物整个冬天都在生长。
senses.why: Sunlight is natural; a lamp copies its work, so the copy is artificial light.
senses.whyCN: 阳光是天然的；灯复制了它的功能，所以这个复制品就是人造光。

senses.title: Insincere or forced
senses.definition: lacking genuine feeling, and therefore forced or false in manner
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏真实情感，因而显得勉强或虚假
senses.example: His artificial smile made the interview awkward.
senses.exampleCN: 他做作的笑容让面试变得尴尬。
senses.why: A feeling made on purpose, like a crafted object, looks manufactured rather than grown.
senses.whyCN: 刻意做出来的情感像一件加工品，看上去是制造出来的，而不是自然长成的。

senses.title: Caused by human action
senses.definition: created or worsened by people rather than by natural causes, as in artificial scarcity
senses.definitionCN: 由人造成或加剧，而非自然原因，如「人为短缺」
senses.example: The shortage was artificial, created by hoarding.
senses.exampleCN: 这种短缺是人为的，由囤积造成。
senses.why: If people make the condition, it is artificial even when it looks like a natural event.
senses.whyCN: 只要这个局面是人造成的，哪怕看起来像自然现象，也算 artificial。

intro.en: Artificial begins as a phrase meaning made by skill, and only later gains the sense of false.
intro.cn: artificial 起初是「由技艺做成」的短语，后来才添上「虚假」的意思。

items.en: Ars meant skill or craft, and facere meant to make; artifex named the skilled maker.
items.cn: ars 意为技艺或手艺，facere 意为制作，artifex 指有手艺的制作者。

items.en: Artificium named the work of the artifex, and artificialis described what was made by such skill.
items.cn: artificium 指工匠的作品，artificialis 则形容由这种技艺做成的东西。

items.en: Artificiel passed into French with the sense 'made by craft rather than by nature'.
items.cn: artificiel 进入法语，意为「由技艺而非自然做成」。

items.en: English artificial first meant skilfully made, without any suggestion of faking.
items.cn: 英语里的 artificial 最初只表示「制作精巧」，尚无造假之意。

items.en: As machine-made goods spread, the word darkened: artificial came to mean imitation or insincerity.
items.cn: 随着机器制品普及，这个词的意味转暗：artificial 开始表示仿造或不真诚。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same making root; the near-meaning group gathers words for synthetic, fake and forced.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一「制作」词根上的词；近义组收表示合成、虚假与勉强的词。

entries.definition: A clever device or trick, especially one meant to deceive.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「巧妙的手法、诡计」，尤指为欺骗而设。

entries.definition: An object made by human hands, especially one of historical interest.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「人工制品」，尤指有历史价值的器物。

entries.definition: A skilled worker who makes things by hand.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「工匠」，指手工制作器物的熟练工人。

entries.definition: Made by chemical processes rather than from natural materials.
entries.definitionCN: 由化学过程制成，而非取自天然材料。

entries.definition: Not genuine, made to look like something valuable.
entries.definitionCN: 不真，做成看似贵重之物的样子。

entries.definition: Made by people rather than occurring in nature.
entries.definitionCN: 由人制造，而非自然界生成。

entries.definition: Artificial in manner, adopted to impress others.
entries.definitionCN: 举止做作，为给人好印象而装出来的。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from plastic flowers to lamps, forced smiles and shortages people create.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子从塑料花走到灯光、强作出的笑容与人制造出的短缺。

normal.en: Artificial petals: the flower was made, not grown.
normal.cn: 人造花瓣：这花是做出来的，不是长出来的。

normal.en: Artificial light: a lamp does the sun's work.
normal.cn: 人造光：灯在做太阳的活儿。

normal.en: Artificial sweetener: chemistry copies sugar.
normal.cn: 人工甜味剂：化学在模仿糖。

normal.en: An artificial smile is put on, not felt.
normal.cn: 做作的笑容是装上去的，不是感受到的。

normal.en: Artificial scarcity: people make the shortage.
normal.cn: 人为短缺：短缺是人造出来的。

abstract.en: Made by art first meant well made, then fake.
abstract.cn: 「由技艺做成」先指做工好，后指虚假。

abstract.en: Everything copied from nature can be called artificial.
abstract.cn: 凡是从自然复制来的东西都叫 artificial。

abstract.en: The word judges the origin, and sometimes the sincerity.
abstract.cn: 这个词判断的是来源，有时也判断真诚。

examples.en: The bouquet looked real until she noticed the artificial petals.
examples.cn: 那束花看上去很真，直到她注意到人造花瓣。

examples.en: Artificial light kept the plants growing all winter.
examples.cn: 人造光让这些植物整个冬天都在生长。

examples.en: His artificial smile made the interview awkward.
examples.cn: 他做作的笑容让面试变得尴尬。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿提非手」——阿提用一只假手代替真手，看着像真的：人造的

root: artificial 由拉丁语 ars「技艺」与 facere「制作」合成 artifex「制作者」，再加 -alis 构成 artificialis，字面就是「由技艺做成的」。英语最初只表示「制作精巧」，后来随着机器制品普及，词义转暗，添上「仿造的、虚假的、做作的」意味；用在 scarcity 这类词上，则指「由人造成而非自然发生的」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses share one origin, made by human skill: a crafted object, a copy of nature, a forced feeling, and a condition people create.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项共享一个来源，即「由人手做成」：经人制作的物件、对自然的复制、强作出的情感，以及人为造成的局面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shop-window bouquet so evenly coloured that every petal looks pressed from a mould.
core.cn: 核心意象：橱窗里颜色过分均匀的一束花，每片花瓣都像模具压出来的。

branches.en: THE CRAFT LINE: anything made by skill is artificial in the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 工艺线：凡由技艺做成的东西，在最古老的意义上都是 artificial。

branches.en: THE IMITATION LINE: a machine takes over the work of nature.
branches.cn: 仿造线：机器接替了自然的工作。

branches.en: THE FACE LINE: a feeling put on shows that it was manufactured.
branches.cn: 表情线：装出来的情感显出它是被制造出来的。

branches.en: THE CAUSE LINE: a shortage made by people is artificial.
branches.cn: 成因线：由人制造的短缺就是人为的。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY LINE: plastic flowers and electric light are both copies made by hand.
branches.cn: 日常线：塑料花与电灯都是人手做出的复制品。

intro.en: Artificial joins the Latin roots for skill and making; its family adds -ly and -ity.
intro.cn: artificial 由表示技艺与制作的两个拉丁词根组合而成，词族再添 -ly 与 -ity。

latinIntro.en: The making root facere also produced artifact and artifice, both naming what a maker turns out.
latinIntro.cn: 表示制作的词根 facere 还生出 artifact 与 artifice，两者都指制作者做出来的东西。

items.meaning: made by human skill, not by nature
items.meaningCN: 由人手做成，而非自然生成
items.example: The lake is artificial, fed by a canal.
items.exampleCN: 这个湖是人工的，由一条运河供水。

items.example: The pond was artificially stocked with fish.
items.exampleCN: 这个池塘的鱼是人工放养的。

items.example: The artificiality of the scene was obvious.
items.exampleCN: 这个场景的做作一目了然。

items.example: The magician's artifice fooled the crowd.
items.exampleCN: 魔术师的机关骗过了人群。

items.meaning: an object made by human hands
items.example: The dig uncovered a bronze artifact.
items.exampleCN: 发掘出土了一件青铜器物。

items.meaning: computer systems that perform tasks needing human-like judgement
items.meaningCN: 能完成需类人判断的任务的计算机系统
items.example: Artificial intelligence now reads many medical scans.
items.exampleCN: 人工智能如今能读许多医学影像。

items.meaning: a replacement for a missing arm or leg

items.exampleCN: 他装上假肢后又可以走路了。

items.meaning: light produced by a device rather than by the sun

items.exampleCN: 温室里亮着人造光。

definition_zh: 艺术家；画家；表演艺术家；能手；（诈骗）高手
definition_en: a person who creates art, a performer, a person highly skilled at something, or, in con artist, a practised trickster
core_image: 沾着颜料的手握画笔，站在画架前退后两步打量自己的画
scene: 画架前的人退后两步，眯起眼睛打量刚完成的那幅肖像。The artist signed her name in the corner of the canvas.
sceneCN: 这里 artist 是「画家、造型艺术家」（第 1 个义项：从事绘画、雕塑等创作的人）；句意为「这位艺术家在画布一角签上了名字」。画面中有画架、画笔与刚完成的肖像。

pos.zh: 名词：艺术家；画家；表演艺术家；能手；诈骗高手

derivatives.zh: artist 的词根，义为「艺术；美术；技艺」
由 artist 加 -ic 构成，义为「艺术的；有艺术气质的」
由 artist 加 -ry 构成，义为「艺术技巧；艺术性」

senses.title: A maker of visual art
senses.definition: a person who creates visual art, such as a painter, sculptor, or printmaker
senses.definitionCN: 创作视觉艺术的人，如画家、雕塑家或版画家
senses.example: The artist signed her name in the corner of the canvas.
senses.exampleCN: 这位艺术家在画布一角签上了名字。
senses.why: The word names the person who practises ars, the Latin skill of making, and visual making is its clearest case.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指 practicing「技艺」的人，而视觉上的制作是这门技艺最清楚的例子。

senses.title: A performer
senses.definition: a person who performs, such as a musician, singer, dancer, or actor, especially in a professional way
senses.definitionCN: 从事表演的人，如音乐家、歌手、舞蹈家或演员，尤指专业者
senses.example: The festival brought artists from a dozen countries.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐节请来了十几个国家的表演艺术家。
senses.why: Skill of the body and voice is also ars, so a stage performer is an artist just as a painter is.
senses.whyCN: 身体与嗓音的技艺同样是技艺，所以舞台表演者和画家一样都是 artist。

senses.title: Someone highly skilled
senses.definition: a person who does something with exceptional skill, often in a stated field
senses.definitionCN: 在某一领域做得极为出色的人，常带说明领域
senses.example: She is an artist with a paintbrush and a knife in the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 她拿起画笔和菜刀都像大师。
senses.why: Since ars once meant any trained skill, anyone who masters a craft can be called an artist.
senses.whyCN: 既然技艺一词本指任何练就的本领，任何把一门手艺练到极致的人都能叫 artist。

senses.title: A practised trickster
senses.definition: in con artist, a person who gains money or trust by deception
senses.definitionCN: 用于 con artist，指靠欺骗获取钱财或信任的人
senses.example: The con artist sold fake tickets outside the stadium.
senses.exampleCN: 那个骗子在体育场外兜售假票。
senses.why: Skill used to deceive becomes craft in the old bad sense, so even a swindler is called an artist.
senses.whyCN: 技艺用于欺骗，就成了古旧意义上的「手腕」，连骗子也被称作 artist。

intro.en: Artist is a Latin word for a practitioner of ars, routed through Italian and French before it reached English.
intro.cn: artist 是拉丁语中「从事技艺之人」的词，经意大利语与法语转手后才进入英语。

items.en: Ars meant skill or craft, and artista named a person devoted to such skill.
items.cn: ars 意为技艺或手艺，artista 指专心从事这种技艺的人。

items.en: In classical use artista could cover a performer or a craftsman, not only a painter.
items.cn: 在古典用法中，artista 可以指表演者或工匠，并不只指画家。

items.en: Italian artista preserved the broad sense of a skilled practitioner during the Renaissance.
items.cn: 文艺复兴时期，意大利语 artista 保留了「有技艺的从业者」这一宽泛含义。

items.en: French artiste narrowed toward the performer, a narrowing that English later partly reversed.
items.cn: 法语 artiste 收窄到指表演者，英语后来又部分地把范围放宽。

items.en: English artist first meant a master of any skill, and only later settled on the visual arts.
items.cn: 英语里的 artist 最初指任何技艺的大师，后来才主要落在视觉艺术上。

items.en: The performer sense lives on, and con artist shows that craft can also mean cunning.
items.cn: 表演者义保留了下来，而 con artist 说明「技艺」也能指狡黠。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same skill root; the near-meaning group gathers makers and performers.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一「技艺」词根上的词；近义组创作者与表演者。

entries.definition: A skilled worker who makes things by hand.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「工匠」，指手工制作器物的熟练工人。

entries.definition: A professional performer, especially a singer or dancer.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「专业表演者」，尤指歌手或舞蹈家。

entries.definition: Relating to art or to artists.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「艺术的；艺术家的」。

entries.definition: A person who paints pictures, or one who paints surfaces.
entries.definitionCN: 画画的人，或给表面刷漆的人。

entries.definition: A person who makes sculptures.
entries.definitionCN: 制作雕塑的人。

entries.definition: A person who entertains an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 为观众表演的人。

entries.definition: A skilled person who makes things by hand.
entries.definitionCN: 以手工制作器物的有技艺者。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a painter at an easel to a stage performer, a skilled cook and a swindler.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子从画架前的画家，走到舞台表演者、手艺高超的厨师与骗子。

normal.en: An artist stands back from the canvas to look.
normal.cn: 艺术家退后两步端详自己的画布。

normal.en: A stage artist performs with body and voice.
normal.cn: 舞台上的艺术家用身体与嗓音表演。

normal.en: An artist with a knife can mean a brilliant cook.
normal.cn: 拿着刀的 artist 也可以指刀工极好的厨师。

normal.en: A con artist practises the craft of cheating.
normal.cn: con artist 练的是骗人的手艺。

normal.en: All of them practise some kind of skill.
normal.cn: 他们都在练某种技艺。

abstract.en: Artist is the person; art is the skill behind the person.
abstract.cn: artist 是人，art 是这个人背后的技艺。

abstract.en: Skill can be turned toward beauty or toward deception.
abstract.cn: 技艺可以朝向美，也可以朝向欺骗。

abstract.en: The word keeps widening and narrowing over the centuries.
abstract.cn: 这个词几百年间不断放宽又收窄。

examples.cn: 这位艺术家在画布一角签上了名字。

examples.cn: 音乐节请来了十几个国家的表演艺术家。

root: artist 来自拉丁语 artista，由 ars（技艺）加 -ista 构成，本指「从事技艺的人」，经意大利语与法语进入英语。它最初可指任何技艺的大师，后来主要落在绘画、雕塑等视觉艺术上；舞台表演因同属技艺，也保留 artist 之名；任何人把一门手艺练到极致都可称 artist；技艺若用于欺骗，则成了 con artist。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses all point to a person of skill: the visual maker, the stage performer, the master of any craft, and the trickster.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都指向「有技艺的人」：视觉创作者、舞台表演者、任何手艺的大师，以及骗子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand stained with paint, holding a brush before an easel.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只沾满颜料的手，握着画笔站在画架前。

branches.en: THE EASEL LINE: the visual maker is the central sense.
branches.cn: 画架线：视觉创作者是这个词的中心义。

branches.en: THE STAGE LINE: body and voice are skills too.
branches.cn: 舞台线：身体与嗓音同样是技艺。

branches.en: THE CRAFT LINE: any mastered skill earns the name.
branches.cn: 手艺线：任何练到极致的本领都配得上这个名字。

branches.en: THE CON LINE: skill bent toward cheating becomes a con artist.
branches.cn: 骗术线：技艺弯向欺骗，就成了 con artist。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY LINE: a serious cook or gardener can be called an artist.
branches.cn: 日常线：认真的厨师或园丁也能被称作 artist。

intro.en: Artist is built on the Latin root ars; its family adds -ic and -ry, and the base word art stands beside it.
intro.cn: artist 建立在拉丁词根 ars 上，词族加 -ic 与 -ry，基础词 art 站在它旁边。

latinIntro.en: The same skill root produced artisan and artifact, both naming people or objects shaped by craft.
latinIntro.cn: 同一个「技艺」词根还生出 artisan 与 artifact，两者都指由手艺塑成的人或物。

items.meaning: the skill or the work produced

items.example: Art needs both skill and patience.

definition_zh: 作为；以…身份；像…一样；当…时；因为；同样地；至于
definition_en: a word used for a role, for comparison, for simultaneous time, for cause, for equality, or in the phrase as for
core_image: 两条平行的线，一条紧跟着另一条往前延伸
scene: 她站在讲台旁，手里拿着名单，示意下一位上台。As the last name was called, she stepped forward.
sceneCN: 这里 as 是连词「当……时」（第 3 个义项：两件事在同一时间发生）；句意为「最后一个名字被叫到时，她走上前」。画面中有讲台、名单与等候上台的人。

pos.zh: 介词：作为；以……身份
连词：像……一样；当……时；因为
副词：同样地；如同

forms.label: 无屈折变化（介词、连词、副词）

derivatives.zh: 由古英语 eallswā「完全如此」缩合而来，与 as 同源，义为「也」
与 as 同出古英语 swā，义为「如此」，是 as 的同源指示词

senses.title: In the role of
senses.definition: used before a noun to show the role, function, or job of a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，表示某人或某物所担任的角色、功能或职务
senses.example: She works as a nurse at the local clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 她在当地诊所当护士。
senses.why: The older English phrase meant 'all so, wholly in that manner', and from it grows the idea of standing in a role.
senses.whyCN: 古英语短语本义是「完全如此、全然以那种方式」，由此长出「处在某个角色中」的意思。

senses.title: Like something else
senses.definition: used to compare two things, showing that they are similar in some way
senses.definitionCN: 用于比较两件事物，表示它们在某个方面相似
senses.example: He is as tall as his father.
senses.exampleCN: 他和他父亲一样高。
senses.why: Two things are placed on parallel lines, and the second is measured against the first.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西被放到两条平行线上，第二样照着第一样来量。

senses.title: At the same time as
senses.definition: used to introduce an event that happens while another event is happening
senses.definitionCN: 用于引出与另一件事同时发生的事件
senses.example: As the last name was called, she stepped forward.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一个名字被叫到时，她走上前。
senses.why: The two parallel lines now run at the same moment, so one event is read alongside the other.
senses.whyCN: 两条平行线此时在同一时刻延伸，于是一个事件就与另一个并排着读。

senses.title: Because
senses.definition: used to give the reason for something, especially at the start of a clause
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明某事的原因，尤见于从句开头
senses.example: As it was raining, we stayed indoors.
senses.exampleCN: 因为在下雨，我们留在了室内。
senses.why: Two lines move together, and the first is treated as the cause that carries the second along.
senses.whyCN: 两条线一起移动，前一条被当作推动后一条的原因。

senses.title: Equally, in the same degree
senses.definition: used in the pattern as ... as to show that two things are equal in some quality
senses.definitionCN: 用于 as ... as 结构，表示两物在某性质上程度相等
senses.example: Please reply as soon as you can.
senses.exampleCN: 请尽快回复。
senses.why: The word marks the point where two measures meet on the same level.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标出两个尺度在同一高度相遇的那一点。

senses.title: Turning to a new topic
senses.definition: in the phrases as for or as to, used to introduce a new subject
senses.definitionCN: 用于 as for 或 as to，引出新的话题
senses.example: As for the bill, we will settle it tomorrow.
senses.exampleCN: 至于账单，我们明天再结。
senses.why: The comparison word is used to set a topic beside the others and say, now look at this one.
senses.whyCN: 这个表示比较的词把某个话题放到其他话题旁边，意思是「现在看这一个」。

intro.en: As is a worn-down Old English phrase meaning 'all so', and its many uses all come from that one comparison.
intro.cn: as 是古英语短语「完全如此」磨损后的形式，它众多用法都源自同一个比较。

items.en: 「*allaz」 meant 'all' and 「*swa」 meant 'so'; together they formed a phrase of full comparison.
items.cn: 「*allaz」意为「全部」，「*swa」意为「如此」，两者合起来构成一个表完全比较的短语。

items.en: Eallswā 'all so, just as' was used for comparison and for manner.
items.cn: eallswā「完全如此、正如」既用于比较，也用于表示方式。

items.en: The phrase wore down to als, alse and as, losing its first element.
items.cn: 这个短语磨损成 als、alse 与 as，前面的成分逐渐脱落。

items.en: As took over the comparison and time senses, while also and so kept the older 'all so' meanings.
items.cn: as 接下了比较与时间义，而 also 与 so 保留了旧的「完全如此」之意。

items.en: The role sense, the reason sense and fixed phrases such as as for all grew from the same stock.
items.cn: 角色义、原因义以及 as for 这类固定短语，都从同一个来源长出来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words that differ from as by a letter; the near-meaning group gathers function words it often replaces.
note.cn: 形近组收与 as 只差一个字母的短词；近义组收它经常替代的那些功能词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow as from a role to a comparison, shared time, a cause, equal degree and a new topic.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子让 as 从角色走到比较、同时、原因、同等程度与新话题。

normal.cn: as tall as：两条线在同一高度。

normal.cn: as it rained：两件事并排发生。

abstract.cn: 一个表示比较的词长出了六种语法职能。

abstract.en: Parallel lines are the picture behind every use.
abstract.cn: 平行线是每一种用法背后的图像。

abstract.en: Role, time and cause are all ways of lining two things up.
abstract.cn: 角色、时间与原因，都是把两样东西排到一条线上的方式。

root: as 是古英语短语 eallswā「完全如此、正如」磨损后的形式，前面的 eall 脱落，只剩 swā 的弱化形，于是成了 as。它由「完全像那样」这一比较义出发，长出一整族语法职能：表示角色（作为）、比较（像……一样）、同时（当……时）、原因（因为）、同等程度（as ... as），以及引出新话题的 as for。同源的 also 与 so 保留了更早的「也、如此」之意。

sensesIntro.en: Six uses all come from one comparison: standing in a role, resembling, happening together, causing, matching in degree, and turning to a topic.
sensesIntro.cn: 六种用法都出自同一个比较：处在角色中、相像、同时发生、构成原因、程度相等，以及转向某个话题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two parallel lines, the second following the first.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条平行的线，第二条紧跟着第一条。

branches.en: THE ROLE LINE: a person is placed in a function.
branches.cn: 角色线：人被放进某个职能里。

branches.en: THE COMPARISON LINE: two things are measured side by side.
branches.cn: 比较线：两样东西并排着量。

branches.en: THE TIME LINE: two events run at the same moment.
branches.cn: 时间线：两个事件在同一时刻延伸。

branches.en: THE CAUSE LINE: the first event carries the second.
branches.cn: 原因线：前一个事件带着后一个走。

branches.en: THE MEASURE LINE: equal degree, or a topic set beside the others.
branches.cn: 尺度线：程度相等，或把话题放到其他话题旁边。

intro.en: As is a function word with almost no morphology; its family is the set of fixed phrases it forms.
intro.cn: as 是几乎没有形态变化的功能词，它的词族就是由它构成的固定短语。

latinIntro.en: As has no Latin layer; the nearest relatives are the native English so and also.
latinIntro.cn: as 没有拉丁层，最近的亲属是本土英语的 so 与 also。

items.exampleCN: 照我说的做。

items.example: As for the cost, we can share it.
items.exampleCN: 至于费用，我们可以分摊。

items.example: He spoke as if he had been there.
items.exampleCN: 他讲得好像自己当时在场。

items.example: She looked as though she had seen a ghost.
items.exampleCN: 她看上去像见了鬼。

definition_zh: 羞愧的；惭愧的；不好意思的；不愿承认的
definition_en: feeling shame or embarrassment about one's own actions, about a situation, or about admitting something
core_image: 低着头、脸发烫，恨不得躲到桌子底下
scene: 教室后排的男孩低着头，手指绞着衣角，不敢看讲台上的老师。He felt ashamed of lying to his best friend.
sceneCN: 这里 ashamed 是「羞愧的」（第 1 个义项：因自己的行为而感到羞耻）；句意为「他因对最好的朋友撒谎而感到羞愧」。画面中有教室后排、低头的男孩与绞着衣角的手。

pos.zh: 形容词：羞愧的；惭愧的；不好意思的；不愿承认的

derivatives.zh: ashamed 的词根名词，义为「羞耻；羞愧；憾事」
由 shame 加 -ful 构成，义为「可耻的；丢脸的」
由 shame 加 -less 构成，义为「无耻的；不知羞耻的」

senses.title: Feeling shame for one's own act
senses.definition: feeling shame or guilt because of something one has done
senses.definitionCN: 因自己做过的事而感到羞耻或内疚
senses.example: He felt ashamed of lying to his best friend.
senses.exampleCN: 他因对最好的朋友撒谎而感到羞愧。
senses.why: The word is a past participle, as if shame had been poured over the person and left him covered.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是过去分词，好像羞耻被浇在这个人身上，让他浑身都罩着它。

senses.title: Embarrassed by a situation
senses.definition: feeling embarrassed about a situation, especially one caused by others or by one's family
senses.definitionCN: 因某种处境、尤指由他人或家人造成的处境而感到难堪
senses.example: She was ashamed of her family's noisy quarrel.
senses.exampleCN: 她为家里那场吵闹的争吵感到难堪。
senses.why: Shame does not need to be earned: whatever places you in the wrong light can cover you too.
senses.whyCN: 羞耻不必是自己挣来的：任何把你放到不光彩位置的事，都能把羞耻罩到你身上。

senses.title: Unwilling to admit something
senses.definition: reluctant to admit or reveal something because it feels humiliating
senses.definitionCN: 因觉得丢脸而不愿承认或透露某事
senses.example: He was ashamed to admit that he had failed.
senses.exampleCN: 他不好意思承认自己失败了。
senses.why: To admit is to stand uncovered before others, and the ashamed person refuses that exposure.
senses.whyCN: 承认就是把自己毫无遮掩地站到人前，而羞愧的人拒绝这种暴露。

intro.en: Ashamed is literally 'shamed', a past participle built on the Old English word for shame.
intro.cn: ashamed 字面就是「被羞耻覆盖的」，是建立在古英语「羞耻」一词上的过去分词。

items.en: 「*skamō」 meant 'shame, disgrace' and is the common source of the Germanic shame words.
items.cn: 「*skamō」意为「羞耻、丢脸」，是各日耳曼语中「羞耻」词的共同来源。

items.en: Scamu meant 'shame, modesty', and the verb scamian meant 'to feel shame'.
items.cn: scamu 意为「羞耻、羞怯」，动词 scamian 意为「感到羞耻」。

items.en: The noun became shame, and a derived verb ashame meant 'to make ashamed'.
items.cn: 名词演变为 shame，又派生出一个动词 ashame，意为「使羞愧」。

items.en: The past participle ashamed outlived the verb and became an adjective in its own right.
items.cn: 过去分词 ashamed 比动词活得更久，本身变成了形容词。

items.en: The modern word covers guilt over one's acts, embarrassment at circumstances, and reluctance to admit.
items.cn: 现代用法涵盖对自己行为的愧疚、对处境的难堪，以及不愿承认。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same shame root; the near-meaning group gathers feelings of embarrassment and guilt.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一「羞耻」词根上的词；近义组收难堪与愧疚一类的感受。

entries.definition: The painful feeling of having done something wrong or foolish.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「羞耻、羞愧」，因做错事或做了蠢事而痛苦的感觉。

entries.definition: Deserving shame or disgrace.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可耻的、丢脸的」。

entries.definition: Pale grey, like ash, often from shock or illness.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「灰白的」，常因震惊或疾病而脸色发灰。

entries.definition: Feeling awkward and self-conscious in front of others.
entries.definitionCN: 在他人面前感到难堪、不自在。

entries.definition: Feeling responsible for wrongdoing.
entries.definitionCN: 因做错事而感到负有责任。

entries.definition: Made to feel foolish or powerless in public.
entries.definitionCN: 在众人面前被弄得愚蠢或无力。

entries.definition: Extremely embarrassed or ashamed.
entries.definitionCN: 极度难堪或羞愧的。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a bowed head to a family quarrel and a refusal to admit.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子从低下的头，走到家里的争吵与不愿承认。

normal.en: Ashamed: the face is hot and the eyes drop.
normal.cn: ashamed：脸发烫，眼睛往下掉。

normal.en: Ashamed of a lie: the act is yours.
normal.cn: 为谎言羞愧：那件事是你做的。

normal.en: Ashamed of a quarrel: the scene is not yours, but it covers you.
normal.cn: 为争吵难堪：场面不是你造成的，却罩住了你。

normal.en: Ashamed to admit: standing uncovered is too much.
normal.cn: 不好意思承认：毫无遮掩地站着太难了。

normal.en: Shame is poured over the person like water.
normal.cn: 羞耻像水一样浇在这个人身上。

abstract.en: Shame can come from your own act or from your surroundings.
abstract.cn: 羞耻可以来自自己的行为，也可以来自周围的环境。

abstract.en: Admitting something feels like being seen without cover.
abstract.cn: 承认某事就像被人看见自己毫无遮掩。

abstract.en: The word is a state, not a deed.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一种状态，不是一个动作。

examples.en: He felt ashamed of lying to his best friend.
examples.cn: 他因对最好的朋友撒谎而感到羞愧。

examples.en: She was ashamed of her family's noisy quarrel.
examples.cn: 她为家里那场吵闹的争吵感到难堪。

examples.en: He was ashamed to admit that he had failed.
examples.cn: 他不好意思承认自己失败了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊，羞的」——他低下头小声说「啊，羞的」：羞愧的

root: ashamed 字面就是「被羞耻覆盖的」：古英语 scamu 意为「羞耻」，动词 scamian 意为「感到羞耻」，中古英语里名词变成 shame，又派生动词 ashame「使羞愧」。它的过去分词 ashamed 活过了动词，独立成形容词。于是它既能指对自己的行为感到羞愧，也能指因处境或他人而难堪，还指因觉得丢脸而不愿承认。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses share the state of being covered by shame: shame for one's own act, embarrassment at a situation, and reluctance to admit.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项共享「被羞耻罩住」这一状态：为自己的行为羞愧、因处境难堪，以及不愿承认。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a head bowed low, a hot face, a wish to hide under the desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：低低的头、发烫的脸，恨不得躲到桌子底下。

branches.en: THE OWN-ACT LINE: shame earned by what one has done.
branches.cn: 己过线：因自己做过的事而挣来的羞耻。

branches.en: THE GAZE LINE: shame brought on by a scene one did not cause.
branches.cn: 目光线：羞耻来自并非自己造成的场面。

branches.en: THE ADMISSION LINE: saying it aloud would leave one uncovered.
branches.cn: 承认线：说出口就等于让自己毫无遮掩。

branches.en: THE HONESTY LINE: a private fault and a public admission pull the same way.
branches.cn: 诚实线：私下的过失与公开的承认，拉的是同一根绳。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL LINE: both the family scene and the refused admission are about being seen.
branches.cn: 社交线：家里的场面与拒绝承认，都关乎「被看见」。

intro.en: Ashamed is a past participle turned adjective; its family is built on the noun shame plus -ful and -less.
intro.cn: ashamed 是过去分词转成的形容词，词族建立在名词 shame 加 -ful 与 -less 上。

latinIntro.en: Shame is a native Germanic word, so there is no Latin family here.
latinIntro.cn: shame 是本土日耳曼词，因此这里没有拉丁词族。

items.example: He was ashamed of his harsh words.
items.exampleCN: 他因自己刻薄的话而羞愧。

items.meaning: the feeling or condition of disgrace
items.example: She hung her head in shame.

items.exampleCN: 那样对待客人真是丢脸。

items.exampleCN: 那个无耻的谎言骗不了任何人。

items.exampleCN: 那位蒙羞的官员立刻辞职了。

items.example: He smiled ashamedly and said nothing.
items.exampleCN: 他羞愧地笑了笑，什么也没说。

items.example: She was unashamed of her accent.
